novelty.result: No dedicated Kula tool narrative found in the searched scope; this is a bounded corpus finding, not an exhaustive absence claim.
existing_overlap: Binchana distinguishes the kula used for winnowing from a hand fan in the 2017 Baripada report.
Dhinki includes winnowing in a Koraput processing sequence but concentrates on pounding.
Essential Odia Dhaga section 13/proverb 46 uses the winnowing tray figuratively to make noise.
novelty.distinct_angle: An independently sourced account of the tray, its use in separating grain and light material, and specifically documented making or work practices can add substantial detail beyond these mentions.

discovery_source.author: Ambika Pattanaik
discovery_source.actual_access: Original page opened; article lines 75–118 read.
discovery_source.role: Topic discovery only. The passing household-object mention does not establish a tool-making process or universal Odisha custom.
discovery_source.independence_boundary: Do not reproduce the festival narrative order, song lines, ritual explanations, images or translated prose.

required_claim_limits: Keep tray operation distinct from pounding, dehusking, threshing and sieving unless the particular source supports the relationship.
Attribute regional materials, shapes, maker groups and dated labour findings to their documented locality and period.
Do not infer pan-Odisha use, ancient origin, extinction, health benefits or a universal ritual role.
A photograph must not identify an unrecorded maker, workshop, locality or material species.
